insights.topic: Verified purchase data vs. probabilistic targeting
insights.insight: The protocol has confirmed $1.294M in real transactions across 21,518 receipts — each one a cryptographically verified purchase event, not an inferred intent signal. For brands paying $5+ CPM for probabilistic audience targeting, this is the structural alternative: deterministic proof of spend, not a model's guess.

Dollar volume has grown faster than receipt count for three consecutive measurement periods, meaning average transaction value is rising even as submission throughput oscillates. Brands should watch whether this reflects higher-value category mix entering the network or existing buyers trading up — either way, the verified spend per user is moving in the right direction.

insights.topic: Early adopter profile: operators, not consumers
insights.insight: All five open vendor integration requests are developer infrastructure — Notion, Vercel, Render, DigitalOcean, Hetzner — zero retail, zero consumer brands. The first wave verifying spend through this protocol is agents and operators tracking operational costs, not mass-market shoppers. Consumer-facing brands are not yet competing for this data layer; that window is still open.

Category entropy holds at 2.985 bits and store entropy at 2.939 bits, with no significant mix shift this period. For marketers, this means the current verified purchase distribution is readable and stable enough to plan against — not a volatile, uninterpretable sample.

After a burst to 23 active CBSAs, the network is holding at 15 active metro cells this period with no new additions. Coverage is real but concentrated — brands with national footprints should treat this as a regional signal source today, not a national panel.

The protocol is designed with no per-wallet visibility — purchase verification is decoupled from individual identity by construction. For CMOs navigating post-cookie compliance requirements, this is the relevant structural fact: verified commerce signals without the personal data liability that comes with traditional identity-linked purchase data.
